description: Authorized penetration test of a web application covering injection, authentication, session management, and access control vulnerabilities.

steps.description: Define the engagement scope, target URLs, testing windows, and obtain written authorization from the asset owner.

inputs.name: target-application
inputs.desc: URL or identifier of the web application to test

inputs.name: authorization-document
inputs.desc: Written permission from the asset owner

outputs.name: engagement-scope
outputs.desc: Defined boundaries including in-scope and out-of-scope targets

outputs.name: rules-of-engagement
outputs.desc: Testing constraints, escalation contacts, and prohibited actions

process: Review the authorization document to confirm testing is permitted for the specified targets.
Define in-scope URLs, IP ranges, and application components.
Set testing windows, escalation procedures, and emergency contacts.
Document prohibited actions and data handling requirements.

steps.description: Enumerate the web application attack surface including endpoints, parameters, authentication flows, and technology stack.

outputs.name: endpoint-inventory
outputs.desc: Complete list of discovered endpoints and their HTTP methods

outputs.name: technology-fingerprint
outputs.desc: Identified server software, frameworks, and libraries

process: Spider the application to discover all reachable endpoints and parameters.
Identify authentication and session management mechanisms.
Fingerprint the technology stack (web server, framework, languages, databases).
Map input vectors including forms, headers, cookies, and URL parameters.

steps.description: Test all input vectors for injection vulnerabilities including SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and command injection.

inputs.name: endpoint-inventory
inputs.desc: List of discovered endpoints and parameters

outputs.name: injection-findings
outputs.desc: List of confirmed injection vulnerabilities with severity ratings

outputs.name: injection-evidence
outputs.desc: Proof-of-concept payloads and response captures for each finding

process: Test each parameter for SQL injection using error-based, blind, and time-based techniques.
Test for reflected and stored cross-site scripting in all input vectors.
Test for command injection, LDAP injection, and XML injection where applicable.
Classify each confirmed finding by severity (critical, high, medium, low).

steps.description: Test authentication mechanisms and session management for weaknesses including brute force, credential stuffing, and session fixation.

inputs.name: injection-findings
inputs.desc: Previously found injection vulnerabilities that may affect auth

outputs.name: auth-findings
outputs.desc: List of authentication and session management vulnerabilities

outputs.name: auth-evidence
outputs.desc: Proof-of-concept demonstrations for each auth finding

process: Test password policies, account lockout, and brute force protections.
Check session token generation for randomness and predictability.
Test for session fixation, session hijacking, and insecure session storage.
Verify logout functionality properly invalidates sessions.

steps.description: Test authorization and access controls for privilege escalation, insecure direct object references, and missing function-level access controls.

inputs.name: auth-findings
inputs.desc: Authentication weaknesses that may enable access control bypass

outputs.name: access-control-findings
outputs.desc: List of authorization bypass vulnerabilities

outputs.name: access-control-evidence
outputs.desc: Proof-of-concept for each access control finding

process: Test horizontal privilege escalation by accessing resources belonging to other users.
Test vertical privilege escalation by attempting admin-level actions from a low-privilege account.
Check for insecure direct object references across all parameterized endpoints.
Verify that all sensitive functions enforce server-side authorization checks.

steps.description: Compile all findings with proof-of-concept evidence, reproduction steps, and risk ratings into a structured format.

outputs.name: consolidated-findings
outputs.desc: All findings with evidence, severity, and CVSS scores

outputs.name: remediation-priorities
outputs.desc: Ordered list of fixes by risk and effort

process: Consolidate all findings from each testing phase into a single inventory.
Assign CVSS scores and business impact ratings to each finding.
Write reproduction steps so the development team can verify each issue.
Prioritize remediation by combining severity with implementation effort.

steps.description: Produce the final penetration test report with executive summary, technical details, and remediation roadmap.

inputs.name: consolidated-findings
inputs.desc: All findings with evidence and CVSS scores

outputs.name: pentest-report
outputs.desc: Complete penetration test report

outputs.name: executive-summary
outputs.desc: One-page summary for non-technical stakeholders

process: Write the executive summary describing overall risk posture and top findings.
Document each finding with technical details, evidence, and remediation guidance.
Include a remediation roadmap with short-term and long-term recommendations.
Append testing methodology, tools used, and scope confirmation.

description: Assess the security of a REST or GraphQL API covering authentication, authorization, rate limiting, input validation, and information disclosure.

steps.description: Inventory all API endpoints, HTTP methods, parameters, and response structures from documentation and active probing.

inputs.name: api-specification
inputs.desc: OpenAPI/Swagger spec, GraphQL schema, or API documentation

inputs.name: api-base-url
inputs.desc: Base URL of the API under test

outputs.name: endpoint-map
outputs.desc: Complete map of endpoints, methods, parameters, and expected responses

outputs.name: auth-requirements
outputs.desc: Authentication requirements for each endpoint

process: Parse the API specification to extract all defined endpoints and methods.
Probe for undocumented endpoints using wordlist-based path enumeration.
Map authentication requirements (API key, OAuth, JWT, none) for each endpoint.
Record expected request and response schemas for validation testing.

steps.description: Test API authentication mechanisms including token generation, expiration, revocation, and cryptographic strength.

inputs.name: endpoint-map
inputs.desc: Map of all endpoints and methods

outputs.name: auth-weaknesses
outputs.desc: List of authentication mechanism vulnerabilities

outputs.name: token-analysis
outputs.desc: Analysis of token structure, entropy, and lifecycle

process: Analyze JWT tokens for weak signing algorithms (none, HS256 with guessable secrets).
Test OAuth flows for redirect URI manipulation and scope escalation.
Verify API key entropy and check for key leakage in logs or responses.
Test token expiration, revocation, and refresh token handling.

steps.description: Test for broken object-level authorization (BOLA/IDOR) and broken function-level authorization across all endpoints.

outputs.name: authorization-findings
outputs.desc: List of authorization bypass vulnerabilities

outputs.name: idor-evidence
outputs.desc: Proof-of-concept for each IDOR finding

process: Test each parameterized endpoint for BOLA by substituting object IDs from other users.
Test function-level authorization by calling admin endpoints with regular user tokens.
Check for mass assignment by sending unexpected fields in create and update requests.
Verify that GraphQL queries enforce field-level authorization.

steps.description: Test rate limiting, throttling, and abuse protection mechanisms on API endpoints.

outputs.name: rate-limit-findings
outputs.desc: Endpoints lacking or with bypassable rate limits

outputs.name: abuse-scenarios
outputs.desc: Documented abuse scenarios for unprotected endpoints

process: Send burst requests to authentication endpoints to test for brute force protection.
Test resource-intensive endpoints for denial-of-service via repeated calls.
Attempt rate limit bypass using header manipulation (X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP).
Document which endpoints have no rate limiting and the potential abuse impact.

steps.description: Test input validation and serialization handling across all API parameters for injection, type confusion, and overflow conditions.

inputs.name: endpoint-map
inputs.desc: Map of endpoints with parameter schemas

inputs.name: rate-limit-findings
inputs.desc: Rate limit status for tested endpoints

outputs.name: input-validation-findings
outputs.desc: List of input validation failures

outputs.name: serialization-findings
outputs.desc: Deserialization and type confusion vulnerabilities

process: Send malformed input types (string where integer expected, nested objects, oversized payloads).
Test for SQL injection, NoSQL injection, and command injection in all parameters.
Check for insecure deserialization in request bodies (JSON, XML, protobuf).
Test boundary conditions (empty strings, null bytes, maximum length values).

steps.description: Check API error responses for information disclosure including stack traces, internal paths, database details, and version information.

inputs.name: input-validation-findings
inputs.desc: Input validation failures that trigger error responses

outputs.name: disclosure-findings
outputs.desc: Information leakage found in error responses

outputs.name: exposed-internals
outputs.desc: Internal details exposed (paths, versions, stack traces)

process: Trigger error conditions on each endpoint and capture the full response.
Check for stack traces, internal file paths, and database query fragments.
Look for version numbers, framework names, and server configuration details.
Verify that production error responses use generic messages without internal details.

steps.description: Produce the API security assessment report with findings, risk ratings, and remediation guidance.

outputs.name: api-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete API security assessment report

outputs.name: remediation-checklist
outputs.desc: Prioritized list of fixes with implementation guidance

process: Consolidate findings from all testing phases with severity ratings.
Map findings to OWASP API Security Top 10 categories.
Write remediation guidance specific to the API framework and architecture.
Produce an executive summary and a detailed technical appendix.

description: Audit cloud infrastructure security across IAM, networking, storage, logging, and compliance with CIS benchmarks.

steps.description: Inventory all cloud resources including compute instances, databases, storage, networking, and serverless functions across accounts and regions.

inputs.name: cloud-account-access
inputs.desc: Read-only credentials or role for the cloud account

outputs.name: resource-inventory
outputs.desc: Complete inventory of all cloud resources by service and region

outputs.name: resource-tags
outputs.desc: Tagging coverage and consistency report

process: Enumerate all resources across every enabled region.
Classify resources by service type, creation date, and last-modified time.
Identify untagged or inconsistently tagged resources.
Flag resources that appear unused (zero traffic, no recent access).

steps.description: Audit IAM policies, roles, and users for overly permissive access, unused credentials, and violations of least privilege.

outputs.name: iam-findings
outputs.desc: List of IAM policy violations and overly permissive roles

outputs.name: unused-credentials
outputs.desc: Credentials and access keys that have not been used recently

process: List all IAM users, roles, groups, and their attached policies.
Identify policies with wildcard permissions (*, Resource: *).
Check for unused credentials and access keys older than 90 days.
Verify that MFA is required for privileged operations and console access.

steps.description: Audit network configurations including VPCs, security groups, NACLs, and firewall rules for excessive exposure.

outputs.name: network-findings
outputs.desc: Network misconfigurations and exposure issues

outputs.name: open-ports-report
outputs.desc: Services exposed to the public internet

process: Map all VPCs, subnets, route tables, and peering connections.
Check security groups for rules allowing 0.0.0.0/0 on sensitive ports.
Identify resources in public subnets that should be private.
Verify that network segmentation isolates production from development.

steps.description: Check permissions on cloud storage resources (S3 buckets, blob containers, GCS buckets) for public access and overly broad sharing.

outputs.name: storage-findings
outputs.desc: Storage misconfigurations and public exposure issues

outputs.name: sensitive-data-exposure
outputs.desc: Storage resources with sensitive data that are publicly accessible

process: Check each storage resource for public access configurations.
Verify bucket policies and ACLs enforce least-privilege access.
Scan for sensitive file patterns (credentials, backups, PII) in public storage.
Check that server-side encryption is enabled for all storage resources.

steps.description: Review logging and monitoring configurations for completeness, covering API activity, network flow logs, and alerting rules.

outputs.name: logging-gaps
outputs.desc: Services and regions missing logging coverage

outputs.name: monitoring-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of alerting rules and incident detection capability

process: Verify that API activity logging (CloudTrail, Activity Log, Audit Log) is enabled in all regions.
Check that network flow logs capture traffic for critical VPCs.
Review alerting rules for coverage of critical security events.
Verify that logs are stored in tamper-resistant, centralized locations.

steps.description: Test cloud configurations against CIS benchmark recommendations for the specific cloud provider.

outputs.name: benchmark-results
outputs.desc: Pass/fail results for each CIS benchmark control

outputs.name: compliance-score
outputs.desc: Overall compliance percentage and breakdown by category

process: Map the provider-specific CIS benchmark controls to testable checks.
Run each check against the current configuration.
Record pass, fail, or not-applicable for each control.
Calculate the compliance score by section and overall.

steps.description: Produce the cloud infrastructure security audit report with findings, compliance status, and remediation priorities.

outputs.name: cloud-audit-report
outputs.desc: Complete cloud security audit report

outputs.name: remediation-roadmap
outputs.desc: Prioritized remediation plan with estimated effort

process: Consolidate all findings with severity, affected resources, and CIS control mapping.
Write the executive summary with overall risk posture and compliance score.
Document each finding with evidence, impact, and specific remediation steps.
Produce a remediation roadmap ordered by risk reduction per unit effort.

description: Review container and orchestration security covering image vulnerabilities, Kubernetes RBAC, network policies, and supply chain integrity.

steps.description: Scan container base images and application images for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and outdated packages.

inputs.name: image-registry
inputs.desc: Container registry URL and access credentials

inputs.name: image-list
inputs.desc: List of container images to scan

outputs.name: image-vulnerabilities
outputs.desc: List of CVEs found in each image with severity

outputs.name: base-image-report
outputs.desc: Base image freshness and update status

process: Pull each image and extract the package manifest.
Scan against CVE databases (NVD, vendor advisories) for known vulnerabilities.
Check base image age and whether newer patched versions exist.
Classify findings by severity and exploitability.

steps.description: Check Dockerfiles for insecure patterns including running as root, hardcoded secrets, and unnecessary packages.

outputs.name: dockerfile-findings
outputs.desc: Insecure patterns found in Dockerfiles

outputs.name: hardening-recommendations
outputs.desc: Specific changes to harden each Dockerfile

process: Check for USER directive to confirm the container does not run as root.
Scan for hardcoded secrets, tokens, and credentials in build arguments and environment variables.
Verify that only necessary packages are installed (no build tools in production images).
Check for proper use of multi-stage builds to minimize the attack surface.

steps.description: Audit Kubernetes RBAC configuration for overly permissive roles, cluster-admin bindings, and service account privileges.

outputs.name: rbac-findings
outputs.desc: Overly permissive roles and bindings

outputs.name: service-account-risks
outputs.desc: Service accounts with excessive privileges

process: List all ClusterRoles, Roles, ClusterRoleBindings, and RoleBindings.
Identify roles with wildcard verbs or resources.
Check for unnecessary cluster-admin bindings.
Review default service account permissions in each namespace.

steps.description: Test Kubernetes network policies for proper pod-to-pod isolation and egress restrictions.

outputs.name: network-policy-findings
outputs.desc: Missing or ineffective network policies

outputs.name: pod-connectivity-map
outputs.desc: Actual pod-to-pod connectivity matrix

process: List all NetworkPolicy resources and their rules.
Identify namespaces and pods with no network policies (default allow-all).
Test actual connectivity between pods to verify policy enforcement.
Check egress policies to confirm pods cannot reach unintended external services.

steps.description: Check how secrets are stored, rotated, and accessed in the container environment.

outputs.name: secrets-findings
outputs.desc: Insecure secret storage and access patterns

outputs.name: rotation-status
outputs.desc: Secret rotation compliance and age report

process: Check for secrets stored as plain Kubernetes Secrets (base64, not encrypted at rest).
Verify that etcd encryption is enabled for secret storage.
Review which pods and service accounts can access which secrets.
Check secret age and rotation policies.

steps.description: Review the container supply chain for image signing, registry access controls, and build pipeline integrity.

outputs.name: supply-chain-findings
outputs.desc: Supply chain integrity issues

outputs.name: signing-status
outputs.desc: Image signing and verification status

process: Check whether images are signed and signatures are verified on pull.
Review registry access controls and who can push images.
Verify that the CI/CD pipeline builds from verified source only.
Check for use of image digests vs mutable tags in deployments.

steps.description: Produce the container security review report with all findings, risk ratings, and hardening recommendations.

outputs.name: container-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete container security report

outputs.name: hardening-plan
outputs.desc: Prioritized hardening actions

process: Consolidate findings from image, Dockerfile, RBAC, network, secrets, and supply chain reviews.
Assign severity ratings based on exploitability and blast radius.
Write specific hardening recommendations for each finding.
Produce a phased hardening plan ordered by risk reduction.

description: Authorized network penetration test covering discovery, service enumeration, vulnerability exploitation, lateral movement, and segmentation validation.

steps.description: Define the network penetration test scope, rules of engagement, target IP ranges, and obtain authorization.

inputs.name: target-network
inputs.desc: IP ranges and network segments to test

outputs.name: network-scope
outputs.desc: In-scope and out-of-scope IP ranges and systems

outputs.name: engagement-rules
outputs.desc: Testing constraints, escalation contacts, and test windows

process: Review authorization to confirm all target ranges are explicitly permitted.
Define testing windows and notification procedures.
Identify critical systems that require extra caution.
Set escalation procedures for unexpected findings (e.g., active compromise).

steps.description: Discover live hosts, open ports, and network topology within the authorized scope.

outputs.name: host-inventory
outputs.desc: List of live hosts with open ports

outputs.name: network-topology
outputs.desc: Observed network topology and segmentation boundaries

process: Run host discovery scans (ICMP, TCP SYN, ARP) across all in-scope ranges.
Perform port scans on discovered hosts (top 1000 TCP and UDP ports).
Map observed network topology including subnets, gateways, and VLANs.
Identify operating systems through TCP/IP fingerprinting.

steps.description: Identify services, versions, and configurations running on discovered hosts and open ports.

outputs.name: service-inventory
outputs.desc: Services with versions and configurations per host

outputs.name: version-vulnerabilities
outputs.desc: Known CVEs matching identified service versions

process: Run service version detection probes on all open ports.
Grab banners and enumerate service configurations.
Cross-reference identified versions against CVE databases.
Identify default credentials and misconfigurations in exposed services.

steps.description: Attempt exploitation of identified vulnerabilities to confirm they are real and to assess impact.

outputs.name: exploitation-results
outputs.desc: Confirmed exploitable vulnerabilities with access level achieved

outputs.name: exploitation-evidence
outputs.desc: Screenshots and logs proving exploitation

process: Prioritize exploitation attempts by CVSS score and network position.
Attempt exploitation of each confirmed vulnerability using proof-of-concept code.
Document the access level achieved (user, root, service account).
Capture evidence (screenshots, command output) for each successful exploitation.

steps.description: Attempt lateral movement from compromised hosts to other network segments to test internal segmentation.

outputs.name: lateral-movement-paths
outputs.desc: Paths from initial compromise to other segments

outputs.name: credential-findings
outputs.desc: Credentials or tokens recovered during movement

process: From each compromised host, enumerate accessible network segments.
Test for credential reuse across systems.
Attempt to pivot through trust relationships (SSH keys, Kerberos tickets, cached credentials).
Document each hop in the lateral movement chain with timestamps.

steps.description: Test network segmentation controls by attempting to cross trust boundaries between defined network zones.

outputs.name: segmentation-findings
outputs.desc: Segmentation failures and bypass paths

outputs.name: firewall-rule-gaps
outputs.desc: Firewall rules that allow unintended cross-zone traffic

process: Test connectivity between network zones (production, development, DMZ, management).
Identify firewall rules that allow broad or unnecessary cross-zone access.
Test VLAN hopping and other layer-2 segmentation bypasses.
Verify that management networks are isolated from user and production networks.

steps.description: Produce the network penetration test report with attack narrative, findings, and remediation priorities.

outputs.name: network-pentest-report
outputs.desc: Complete network penetration test report

outputs.name: attack-narrative
outputs.desc: Step-by-step narrative of the attack path from entry to objective

process: Write the attack narrative showing the full path from initial access to final objective.
Consolidate all findings with severity, affected hosts, and evidence.
Map findings to the MITRE ATT&CK framework for context.
Produce a remediation plan prioritized by position in the attack chain.

description: Review source code for security vulnerabilities using static analysis, manual review, dependency checking, and business logic testing.

steps.description: Inventory the codebase and identify high-risk areas including authentication, authorization, data handling, and cryptographic operations.

inputs.name: source-repository
inputs.desc: Repository URL or local path to the codebase

inputs.name: application-context
inputs.desc: Description of the application purpose and architecture

outputs.name: risk-inventory
outputs.desc: Map of high-risk code areas with threat context

outputs.name: technology-stack
outputs.desc: Languages, frameworks, and libraries in use

process: Catalog all source files by language, framework, and function.
Identify code handling authentication, authorization, and session management.
Locate code that processes user input, performs database queries, or calls external services.
Mark areas using cryptographic operations, file I/O, or system commands.

steps.description: Run static analysis security testing (SAST) tools against the codebase and triage the results.

inputs.name: risk-inventory
inputs.desc: High-risk code areas to focus on

outputs.name: sast-findings
outputs.desc: Triaged SAST findings filtered for true positives

outputs.name: false-positive-log
outputs.desc: False positives with justification for exclusion

process: Configure and run SAST tools appropriate for the technology stack.
Triage each finding to separate true positives from false positives.
Assign severity based on exploitability and data sensitivity.
Document false positive rationale for future scan tuning.

steps.description: Manually review flagged code paths for vulnerabilities that static analysis cannot detect, including race conditions and logic errors.

inputs.name: sast-findings
inputs.desc: SAST results to guide manual review

outputs.name: manual-review-findings
outputs.desc: Vulnerabilities found through manual code review

outputs.name: code-quality-notes
outputs.desc: Security-relevant code quality observations

process: Trace data flows from user input to sensitive operations (sinks).
Check for race conditions in concurrent code paths.
Review error handling for information leakage and fail-open conditions.
Verify that security controls are applied consistently across similar code paths.

steps.description: Test for business logic vulnerabilities that bypass security through legitimate application flows used in unintended sequences.

outputs.name: logic-flaw-findings
outputs.desc: Business logic vulnerabilities found

outputs.name: abuse-case-descriptions
outputs.desc: Step-by-step abuse cases for each logic flaw

process: Identify state machines and multi-step workflows in the application.
Test for step-skipping, parameter tampering, and race conditions in workflows.
Check for price manipulation, quantity overflow, and discount stacking in e-commerce flows.
Verify that business rules are enforced server-side, not only client-side.

steps.description: Check all third-party dependencies and their transitive dependencies against known CVE databases.

inputs.name: source-repository
inputs.desc: Repository with lock files and manifests

outputs.name: dependency-vulnerabilities
outputs.desc: Known CVEs in direct and transitive dependencies

outputs.name: upgrade-recommendations
outputs.desc: Recommended version upgrades to resolve CVEs

process: Parse all dependency manifests and lock files (package.json, requirements.txt, go.mod, etc.).
Resolve the full dependency tree including transitive dependencies.
Cross-reference each dependency version against NVD and vendor advisory databases.
Identify the minimum version upgrade path to resolve each CVE.

steps.description: Verify that the codebase follows secure coding standards for the language and framework in use.

outputs.name: coding-standard-gaps
outputs.desc: Deviations from secure coding standards

outputs.name: pattern-recommendations
outputs.desc: Recommended secure coding patterns to adopt

process: Check for use of parameterized queries vs string concatenation in database operations.
Verify output encoding in all rendering contexts (HTML, JavaScript, URL, CSS).
Check cryptographic implementations for known weak patterns (ECB mode, static IVs, weak hashing).
Verify that secrets are loaded from environment or vault, not hardcoded.

steps.description: Produce the source code security review report with all findings, code locations, and fix guidance.

outputs.name: code-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete source code security review report

outputs.name: fix-priority-list
outputs.desc: Prioritized list of fixes with code-level guidance

process: Consolidate all findings with file paths, line numbers, and severity ratings.
Write fix guidance with before/after code examples for each finding category.
Produce a summary of systemic issues vs one-off findings.
Recommend process improvements (linting rules, pre-commit hooks) to prevent recurrence.

description: Authorized social engineering assessment covering phishing simulations, phone pretexting, and physical security testing.

steps.description: Define the social engineering assessment scope, approved scenarios, and obtain management authorization.

inputs.name: organization-profile
inputs.desc: Company name, industry, and employee count

inputs.name: management-authorization
inputs.desc: Written approval for social engineering testing

outputs.name: approved-scenarios
outputs.desc: List of approved attack scenarios with constraints

outputs.name: target-groups
outputs.desc: Employee groups selected for testing

process: Review management authorization for scope boundaries and prohibited techniques.
Select employee groups for testing across departments and seniority levels.
Define success criteria and metrics for each scenario.
Establish a safe word and immediate stop procedures.

steps.description: Prepare pretexting materials including phishing emails, landing pages, phone scripts, and physical props.

outputs.name: phishing-materials
outputs.desc: Email templates and landing pages for phishing campaigns

outputs.name: pretext-scripts
outputs.desc: Phone and in-person pretext scripts

process: Research the organization's communication style, email format, and common vendors.
Create phishing email templates matching internal communication patterns.
Build credential harvesting landing pages that mimic legitimate login portals.
Write phone pretext scripts for common scenarios (IT support, vendor, executive).

steps.description: Execute phishing email campaigns against target groups and track open rates, click rates, and credential submissions.

outputs.name: phishing-metrics
outputs.desc: Open rate, click rate, and credential submission rate per campaign

outputs.name: reporter-metrics
outputs.desc: Rate at which employees reported the phishing attempt

process: Deploy the phishing infrastructure (sending domain, tracking, landing pages).
Send phishing emails to target groups according to the approved schedule.
Track email opens, link clicks, credential submissions, and attachment downloads.
Record which employees reported the email through proper channels.

steps.description: Execute phone-based pretexting calls to test employee resistance to social engineering over the phone.

outputs.name: phone-test-results
outputs.desc: Success/failure rate and information disclosed per call

outputs.name: call-transcripts
outputs.desc: Anonymized summaries of each test call

process: Place calls using approved pretext scenarios (IT help desk, vendor, executive request).
Record what information was disclosed (credentials, internal systems, org chart details).
Note which employees challenged the caller or escalated to security.
Document the elapsed time and number of attempts needed for each successful pretext.

steps.description: Test physical security controls including tailgating, badge cloning, and access to restricted areas.

outputs.name: physical-test-results
outputs.desc: Success/failure of each physical access attempt

outputs.name: physical-evidence
outputs.desc: Photographs and notes from physical testing (no PII)

process: Attempt to tailgate through secured entrances during approved testing windows.
Test badge reader controls by presenting cloned or invalid credentials.
Attempt to access server rooms, network closets, and restricted floors.
Document the response of security personnel and employees to each attempt.

steps.description: Measure the organization's detection and reporting rate across all social engineering channels.

outputs.name: detection-rates
outputs.desc: Detection and reporting rates by channel and department

outputs.name: response-time-metrics
outputs.desc: Time from attack to detection and from detection to response

process: Calculate detection rate for each channel (email, phone, physical).
Measure time from attack initiation to first employee report.
Measure time from employee report to security team response.
Break down detection rates by department and role level.

steps.description: Produce the social engineering assessment report with metrics, findings, and training recommendations.

outputs.name: social-engineering-report
outputs.desc: Complete social engineering assessment report

outputs.name: training-recommendations
outputs.desc: Targeted security awareness training recommendations

process: Summarize metrics across all channels with comparisons to industry benchmarks.
Identify the most effective attack vectors and the most vulnerable groups.
Write targeted training recommendations for the highest-risk departments.
Propose process improvements (reporting button, verification procedures) based on findings.

description: Test mobile application security on iOS and Android covering binary analysis, data storage, network traffic, and platform-specific controls.

steps.description: Decompile and analyze the mobile application binary for hardcoded secrets, obfuscation level, and code structure.

inputs.name: application-binary
inputs.desc: APK (Android) or IPA (iOS) file to analyze

outputs.name: binary-analysis-results
outputs.desc: Decompiled code analysis findings

outputs.name: obfuscation-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of code obfuscation and anti-tampering protections

process: Decompile the binary (jadx for Android, class-dump/Hopper for iOS).
Search for hardcoded API keys, secrets, tokens, and credentials.
Assess obfuscation level and identify any anti-tampering or root/jailbreak detection.
Map the application's internal structure, libraries, and third-party SDKs.

steps.description: Test how the application stores data locally including keychain/keystore usage, shared preferences, SQLite databases, and file system storage.

outputs.name: storage-findings
outputs.desc: Insecure local data storage findings

outputs.name: sensitive-data-map
outputs.desc: Map of where sensitive data is stored on the device

process: Check iOS Keychain and Android Keystore usage for credential storage.
Examine shared preferences and UserDefaults for sensitive data in plaintext.
Query SQLite databases for stored credentials, tokens, and personal data.
Check the application sandbox for sensitive files, logs, and cached data.

steps.description: Intercept and analyze the application's network traffic for insecure communications, sensitive data exposure, and API vulnerabilities.

outputs.name: traffic-findings
outputs.desc: Network security findings from traffic analysis

outputs.name: api-endpoints-discovered
outputs.desc: API endpoints and their authentication mechanisms

process: Configure a proxy (Burp, mitmproxy) to intercept application traffic.
Check for HTTP connections transmitting sensitive data without TLS.
Analyze API requests for sensitive data in URLs, headers, or unencrypted bodies.
Test for proper server certificate validation.

steps.description: Test the application's certificate pinning implementation for bypass vulnerabilities.

outputs.name: pinning-findings
outputs.desc: Certificate pinning bypass results

outputs.name: pinning-implementation-notes
outputs.desc: Details of the pinning implementation and its strength

process: Attempt to intercept traffic using a custom CA certificate.
If pinning is present, attempt bypass using common techniques (Frida, SSL Kill Switch).
Verify whether pinning covers all network connections or only some endpoints.
Check for pinning on both the leaf certificate and the intermediate/root chain.

steps.description: Scan the decompiled application and its resources for hardcoded API keys, encryption keys, and credentials.

outputs.name: secrets-found
outputs.desc: Hardcoded secrets with location and type

outputs.name: secret-exposure-impact
outputs.desc: Impact assessment for each exposed secret

process: Search decompiled code for API key patterns (string entropy, known prefixes).
Check resource files, configuration files, and build artifacts for embedded secrets.
Test any discovered API keys against their respective services to confirm they are active.
Assess the impact of each exposed secret (data access, financial, reputational).

steps.description: Test deep link and intent handling for vulnerabilities including unauthorized data access and code execution through malicious URIs.

inputs.name: binary-analysis-results
inputs.desc: Code analysis showing registered URI schemes and intents

outputs.name: deep-link-findings
outputs.desc: Deep link and intent handling vulnerabilities

outputs.name: uri-attack-surface
outputs.desc: Map of registered URI schemes and their handlers

process: Enumerate all registered URL schemes, universal links, and intent filters.
Test each handler with malformed and malicious input.
Check for authorization bypass through direct deep link access to protected screens.
Test for data exfiltration through crafted intents or URL parameters.

steps.description: Produce the mobile application security test report with platform-specific findings and remediation guidance.

outputs.name: mobile-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete mobile security test report

outputs.name: platform-remediation-guide
outputs.desc: Platform-specific remediation guidance

process: Consolidate findings from all testing phases with platform-specific context.
Map findings to OWASP Mobile Top 10 categories.
Write remediation guidance using platform-native security APIs (Keychain, Keystore, App Transport Security).
Produce a risk-prioritized fix list with estimated development effort.

description: Assess wireless network security covering encryption, authentication, rogue access points, client isolation, and guest segmentation.

steps.description: Discover all wireless access points, their SSIDs, channels, encryption types, and signal strengths within the authorized test area.

inputs.name: test-location
inputs.desc: Physical location and boundaries for wireless testing

outputs.name: access-point-inventory
outputs.desc: All detected access points with SSID, BSSID, channel, and encryption

outputs.name: signal-coverage-map
outputs.desc: Signal strength and coverage area for each access point

process: Scan all wireless channels (2.4 GHz and 5 GHz) for beacon frames.
Record SSID, BSSID, channel, encryption type, and signal strength for each AP.
Identify organization-owned vs unknown access points.
Map signal coverage boundaries to identify leakage outside the premises.

steps.description: Test the encryption strength of wireless networks including WPA2/WPA3 configuration and known protocol weaknesses.

inputs.name: access-point-inventory
inputs.desc: Detected access points and their encryption types

outputs.name: encryption-findings
outputs.desc: Encryption weaknesses and misconfigurations found

outputs.name: protocol-analysis
outputs.desc: Analysis of wireless protocol security per network

process: Identify networks using deprecated protocols (WEP, WPA-TKIP).
Check WPA2 networks for PMKID vulnerability and known key reinstallation attacks.
Verify WPA3 networks for proper SAE implementation.
Test for downgrade attacks from WPA3 to WPA2 on transition-mode networks.

steps.description: Test wireless authentication mechanisms on authorized test networks using dictionary and brute force techniques.

outputs.name: auth-attack-results
outputs.desc: Results of authentication attack attempts

outputs.name: weak-credentials
outputs.desc: Any weak or default credentials discovered

process: Capture the WPA handshake or PMKID from the authorized test network.
Run dictionary attacks using common password lists against the captured material.
Test for WPS PIN brute force on any access points with WPS enabled.
Check enterprise networks (802.1X) for certificate validation and EAP downgrade attacks.

steps.description: Detect rogue access points, evil twins, and unauthorized wireless devices within the organization's premises.

outputs.name: rogue-ap-findings
outputs.desc: Unauthorized access points and evil twins detected

outputs.name: rogue-ap-locations
outputs.desc: Approximate physical locations of rogue devices

process: Compare detected BSSIDs against the authorized access point inventory.
Identify access points broadcasting organization SSIDs from unauthorized hardware.
Triangulate approximate physical locations of rogue devices using signal strength.
Check for unauthorized Wi-Fi bridges or repeaters connected to the wired network.

steps.description: Test wireless client isolation to verify that connected clients cannot communicate with or attack other clients on the same network.

outputs.name: isolation-findings
outputs.desc: Client isolation failures and bypass methods

outputs.name: client-to-client-paths
outputs.desc: Confirmed communication paths between wireless clients

process: Connect two test devices to the same SSID and attempt direct communication.
Test ARP spoofing and DHCP starvation on the wireless network.
Check if client isolation is enforced at the AP or only at the controller level.
Test whether isolation can be bypassed through VLAN hopping or routing tricks.

steps.description: Test guest wireless network segmentation to verify it cannot reach internal networks, management interfaces, or other VLANs.

outputs.name: guest-segmentation-findings
outputs.desc: Guest network segmentation failures

outputs.name: reachable-internal-resources
outputs.desc: Internal resources accessible from the guest network

process: From the guest network, scan for reachable internal IP ranges.
Attempt to access management interfaces (AP controllers, switches, printers).
Test DNS resolution of internal hostnames from the guest network.
Verify that captive portal bypass does not grant access to internal resources.

steps.description: Produce the wireless network security assessment report with findings, risk ratings, and hardening recommendations.

outputs.name: wireless-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete wireless security assessment report

outputs.name: wireless-hardening-guide
outputs.desc: Wireless network hardening recommendations

process: Consolidate all findings with severity and affected SSIDs/BSSIDs.
Write the executive summary with the overall wireless risk posture.
Document each finding with evidence, impact, and specific configuration fixes.
Produce a wireless hardening guide covering encryption, authentication, segmentation, and monitoring.

description: Audit database security covering access controls, privileges, encryption, credential strength, and audit logging.

steps.description: Inventory all database instances, versions, and their network exposure across the environment.

inputs.name: environment-scope
inputs.desc: Network ranges and cloud accounts to inventory

inputs.name: database-types
inputs.desc: Database technologies in use (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, etc.)

outputs.name: database-inventory
outputs.desc: All database instances with version, location, and network exposure

outputs.name: patch-status
outputs.desc: Patch level relative to current stable releases

process: Discover database instances through network scanning, cloud APIs, and configuration management.
Record the version, edition, and patch level of each instance.
Determine network exposure (internet-facing, internal-only, VPN-accessible).
Identify instances running end-of-life or unpatched versions.

steps.description: Check database authentication mechanisms for strength, including password policies, network restrictions, and multi-factor requirements.

outputs.name: auth-control-findings
outputs.desc: Authentication weaknesses found

outputs.name: network-access-findings
outputs.desc: Network-level access control issues

process: Check authentication methods (password, certificate, Kerberos, LDAP integration).
Verify that password policies enforce minimum complexity and rotation.
Check network-level access restrictions (listen addresses, pg_hba.conf, bind addresses).
Test for anonymous or unauthenticated access to any database instance.

steps.description: Review user privileges across all database instances for least privilege violations and excessive grants.

outputs.name: privilege-findings
outputs.desc: Excessive privileges and least-privilege violations

outputs.name: role-hierarchy-map
outputs.desc: Map of roles, grants, and privilege inheritance

process: List all database users, roles, and their granted privileges.
Identify users with DBA or superuser privileges who do not need them.
Check for application accounts with excessive privileges (DROP, GRANT, ALTER).
Verify that privilege grants follow role-based access control patterns.

steps.description: Test for default credentials, weak passwords, and shared accounts across database instances.

outputs.name: credential-findings
outputs.desc: Default, weak, or shared credentials found

outputs.name: credential-reuse-map
outputs.desc: Instances sharing the same credentials

process: Test for default vendor credentials (sa/blank, root/blank, admin/admin).
Run dictionary attacks against database accounts using common password lists.
Identify shared service accounts used across multiple applications.
Check for credential reuse between development and production instances.

steps.description: Audit database encryption for data at rest (TDE, filesystem encryption) and data in transit (TLS connections).

outputs.name: encryption-findings
outputs.desc: Encryption gaps and misconfigurations

outputs.name: tls-configuration
outputs.desc: TLS version, cipher suites, and certificate status per instance

process: Check whether transparent data encryption (TDE) is enabled for databases containing sensitive data.
Verify TLS is required for all client connections (reject plaintext).
Check TLS configuration for weak protocol versions (TLS 1.0, 1.1) and cipher suites.
Verify that database backups are encrypted.

steps.description: Review database audit logging configuration for completeness, covering DDL, DML, authentication events, and privilege changes.

outputs.name: audit-logging-findings
outputs.desc: Logging gaps and configuration issues

outputs.name: log-retention-status
outputs.desc: Log storage locations and retention periods

process: Check whether audit logging is enabled and capturing DDL statements.
Verify that authentication successes and failures are logged.
Check that privilege escalation and role changes trigger audit events.
Verify that audit logs are stored externally (not only on the database server) and have adequate retention.

steps.description: Produce the database security audit report with all findings, risk ratings, and hardening recommendations.

outputs.name: database-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete database security audit report

outputs.name: database-hardening-checklist
outputs.desc: Instance-specific hardening checklist

process: Consolidate findings across all database instances with severity and affected instance details.
Write instance-specific hardening checklists with exact configuration changes.
Produce the executive summary with overall database risk posture.
Recommend process improvements (automated scanning, privilege reviews, rotation policies).
